summary: Regression backend-only testing after server.py split (1797 → 70 lines) + APScheduler addition. 43/43 new tests pass in /app/backend/tests/test_regression_refactor.py + 13/13 previous notification tests re-run OK. Full endpoint coverage validated: auth, users CRUD w/ self-protection, master data (clients/manufacturers/products), pipeline (leads/opps/proposals/orders), dashboard (kpis, funnel ± manufacturer_id, alerts), analytics (7 endpoints), technical (projects + /me/*), finance flow end-to-end (plan → partial invoice → payment → 2nd invoice → payment → recalc_order_status='fulfilled' → cancel invoice → plan unwind), audit after PATCH, 3 CSV exports, notifications (Resend test-email + digest with RBAC), and scheduler (module imports _job_send_alerts_digest, manual invocation OK, env vars validated, startup log line present).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py split is clean (70 lines, thin bootstrap) — good. Consider adding a health endpoint under /api that pings Mongo instead of only returning static ok:true.
routers/notifications.py `send_alerts_digest` still takes `payload: dict = None` — a Pydantic AlertsDigestRequest{to: Optional[EmailStr]} would give validation + OpenAPI docs.
helpers.send_email_async surfaces raw Resend exception text in HTTP 500 body (f'Resend erro: {str(e)}') — redact to avoid leaking Resend internals.
scheduler.py: type union syntax `AsyncIOScheduler | None` requires Python 3.10+ (ok here — 3.11.15) but worth pinning python_requires in requirements.
deps.py: `require_roles` grants admin implicit access to every role — intentional but should be documented explicitly (it currently reads a bit surprising in the fn body).

seed.py + helpers.build_alerts_digest_html not read this iteration but review request states they are unchanged from the previous monolithic server.py — spot-checked call sites in scheduler.py and notifications.py wire them correctly.
APScheduler runs in-process — for multi-worker deploys (gunicorn -w >1) the digest would fire N times/day. Consider a MongoDB-backed jobstore or a single-worker sidecar.

seed_data_creation: TestFinanceFlow builds a full order via the pipeline (client → opp → convert-to-proposal → patch lines + status=ganha → convert-to-order) using TEST_ prefixed names. All 3 pre-existing seeded orders were already in status=fulfilled from earlier runs, so a fresh order is created per finance-flow test to avoid mutating fulfilled orders. TestUsersManagement creates a user (email test_user_<uuid>@whymob.pt) then deactivates it; not currently cleaned up — negligible.
context_for_next_testing_agent: New comprehensive suite lives at /app/backend/tests/test_regression_refactor.py. Runs in ~5s under pytest-xdist. Two suites now: test_notifications_resend.py (13) + test_regression_refactor.py (43). Both green. Scheduler start log grep is `'[scheduler] iniciado — alerts_digest às 09:00'` in /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log. Manual scheduler dry-run: `cd /app/backend && python -c 'import asyncio; from scheduler import _job_send_alerts_digest; asyncio.run(_job_send_alerts_digest())'` — logs `[scheduler] alerts_digest: sem alertas ativos — nada a enviar` when no active alerts (expected).
